data.name: Harshashree
data.gender_notes: Harshashree is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of prosperity, wisdom, and strength
data.long_meaning: Harshashree is the name of a Hindu goddess, a combination of Harsh (rough) and Ashree (prosperous). She is a symbol of strength and wisdom, who overcomes challenges and brings prosperity. Harshashree is also known as Shree or Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity in Hinduism. She is often depicted with four arms, holding a lotus in two hands and a bell and a conch shell in the other two. Harshashree is also associated with Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and learning. She is often invoked during religious ceremonies and rituals to seek her blessings for wisdom and prosperity.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength, wisdom, and prosperity in Hinduism
data.etymology: Harshashree belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of prosperity, wisdom, and strength.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harshashree total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Harshavardhana's grandson Harshashree succeeded him in 606 CE and continued his dynasty for another 17 years. This period is known as the 'Harshacharma period'. Harshashree is also known as Harshamalla because he was a great patron of arts and letters, just like his grandfather.
historical_references.context: Post-Gupta Empire, Hindu Kingdom of Thanesar (Kanauj)

historical_references.reference: Harshashree was a brilliant military strategist who expanded the borders of the Hindu Kingdom of Thanesar. He is known to have successfully defended against the invading forces of the Turkish General, Shihab-ud-Din Muhammad. This victory ensured the continued existence of the Hindu Kingdom of Thanesar for some time.
historical_references.context: Early medieval India, Wars with invading forces
